faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: Didn't find an answer? Write to us — we reply within a business day.

items.question: How long does it take to launch a project?
items.answer: A first working prototype is usually ready in 4–6 weeks. A full product depends on scope, but we always move in iterations with regular demos.

items.question: Do you work with an existing product?
items.answer: Yes. We run a technical audit, plug into your current codebase and gradually improve the architecture without stopping the business.

items.question: How do you ensure data security?
items.answer: Encryption at every layer, access control, auditing and compliance. For AI solutions, data never leaves your perimeter without approval.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: We support the product under an SLA, watch metrics, resolve incidents and grow functionality along the roadmap.

items.question: How is the cost calculated?
items.answer: It depends on scope, team composition and timeline. After discovery you get a transparent estimate and plan with no hidden fees.

hero.title: Projects we own by results
hero.subtitle: A few examples of how we solve business problems with technology. Placeholder content.

items.title: Next-generation payment platform
items.summary: We re-architected the payment core and moved settlements to real time.
items.challenge: A legacy monolithic core couldn't handle growth, and releases took weeks. They needed an architecture ready to scale to millions of transactions.
items.solution: We split the monolith into services, introduced real-time event processing and built observability. We set up CI/CD for fast, safe releases.

items.title: AI assistant for customer support
items.summary: We deployed an LLM-based assistant that resolves most requests without an operator.
items.challenge: The support team couldn't keep up with growing volume, response times were rising, and operator costs kept increasing.
items.solution: We built an LLM assistant with knowledge-base search (RAG), integrated it with the CRM and set up handoff of complex requests to an operator.

items.title: Digital twin of the factory floor
items.summary: We built a single monitoring panel for equipment with predictive analytics.
items.challenge: Equipment data was scattered, and downtime was discovered after the fact. There was no single picture or forecasting.
items.solution: We unified real-time telemetry, built dashboards and a predictive maintenance model to catch failures early.
